_about: Changes to the Climate Errata website itself (not errata). Newest first. Rendered to updates.html and site-updates.xml by tools/build.py.

updates.title: Lighter-check label and fewer, informational messages to authors
updates.text: "What we checked" now distinguishes papers whose methods we reviewed without rerunning anything ("Method reviewed, not rerun") from those we reproduced or tested. Notes on papers whose authors we have not contacted now describe only what we did and the outcome. Messages to authors are now sent only for findings we have tested ourselves and rate Medium or High; they are for information, ask for no reply, and say that the analysis was AI-assisted and checked by the editor.

updates.title: Clearer rules on author replies and on what an entry claims
updates.text: First messages to authors and producers now say that a finding may be recorded here. Their replies are published, quoted or summarised only with their explicit permission; without it, an entry gives only our own assessment and says that they were contacted. A new section of the Policies page, "What an entry claims", says that every entry is our own assessment, links to its method and code, and that High findings are also written up for a formal, citable outlet.

updates.title: Significance labels now link to how they are scored
updates.text: Every "Significance: High / Medium / Low" label in the register, search results, dataset pages and entry pages now links to the scoring rubric on the About page (size of the effect, reach of the affected paper, dataset or code, and consequence for published results). The register also has a one-line explanation under its filters.

updates.title: New page: What we checked
updates.text: A new page lists every paper, dataset and piece of code we have checked, with the outcome, including the many with no error. Papers (screened systematically since 22 November 2026) are tallied separately for those supporting and those questioning mainstream climate findings. Items whose possible errors are still with the authors, producers or developers are counted but not named until they reply or three weeks pass. The page is in the menu as "What we checked".

updates.title: What we select for review, and where from
updates.text: The How it works page now explains how papers, datasets and code are chosen: most-cited recent papers in five major journals, widely cited papers that question mainstream findings (tested the same way), widely used datasets and open-source climate software. Substack, blogs, news, social media and non-peer-reviewed preprints are out of scope.

updates.title: Each entry now starts with what the dataset, paper or code is
updates.text: Every entry page now opens with a short "What it is" description of the dataset, paper or software concerned, before the finding, and the register shows the same description on each card. Also fixed: on ten entry pages that link to our Zenodo write-ups, the status label at the top wrongly read "Our write-up on Zenodo (latest version)" instead of the entry's status.

updates.title: Fixes we propose; our reports on Zenodo
updates.text: The How it works page now explains the fixes we send with reports: patches and pull requests for software, affected areas and workarounds for datasets, and corrected analyses for papers. It also lists our two broader reports on Zenodo. The home page mentions the proposed fixes too.

updates.title: Entries link to our Zenodo preprints
updates.text: Entries backed by one of our Zenodo preprints now link to it on the entry page. The links use Zenodo's all-versions DOI, so they always open the latest version. Links were added for the modifiedmk, Ali et al. 2026 and Jin & Pu 2026 entries, and the hourly-precipitation entry now opens version 3 rather than version 2.

updates.title: New address: climateerrata.org
updates.text: The site now lives at climateerrata.org. The old address, climate-errata.netlify.app, redirects there automatically, so existing links keep working.

updates.title: Full write-ups for the High-significance entries
updates.text: The 11 entries rated High significance now have full write-ups: what was found, with the key numbers, who is affected, the responsible party's response, what users can do, and how to reproduce the result. The other entries will follow.

updates.title: Fix details on every fixed entry
updates.text: Each fixed entry now shows when the fix was made, which version or pull request contains it, which versions are affected, and whether the fix is retroactive. The register separates fixes that are released from fixes merged but not yet released. Release statuses were rechecked on GitHub and CRAN.

updates.title: Policies and privacy page
updates.text: A new page covers contact first, author responses and disputes, corrections and withdrawals, moderation, a code of conduct, funding and conflicts of interest, use of AI, privacy, and takedown or legal requests. It is linked from the top menu and every page footer.

updates.title: Papers that use the affected data
updates.text: Entries about a problem in a dataset can now list papers that use the affected data for the affected region and period. The effect on each paper is not assessed. The first lists are on the MERRA-2 Australia and ASOS wind entries.

updates.title: Dataset pages
updates.text: A new Datasets section has one page for each of 14 widely used datasets (ERA5, MERRA-2, CPC Unified, GPCC, GPCP, IMERG, E-OBS, ICOADS, HadSST4, OISST, IBTrACS, COOP HPD, ASOS, GHCN-CAMS). Each page gives the current version, the producer's known-issues page and contact, our entries, related discussions, a place to ask questions, and an RSS feed. There is also a feed for the whole register.

updates.title: Discussion by DOI, site search and a contact form
updates.text: Any paper or dataset can now have a discussion page: enter its DOI on Discuss a DOI. Search covers the register, the datasets and the discussions. Write to us takes questions, private error reports and author responses from people without a GitHub account. A posting policy asks that new error claims go to the responsible party first.

updates.title: Climate Errata launched
updates.text: The register of errors found in climate papers, datasets and code moved from its earlier home to this site, with 48 entries, filters, a significance rubric and a comment thread on every entry.
